'''Tim Frazier''' (born November 1, 1990) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[Minas Tênis Clube (basketball)|Minas]] in [[Novo Basquete Brasil]]. Frazier played high school basketball for [[Strake Jesuit College Preparatory]] and competed at the collegiate level with [[Penn State Nittany Lions basketball|Penn State]] as a [[point guard]]. He earned various accolades with Penn State, including first-team [[List of All-Big Ten Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big Ten]] and All-Big Ten Defensive team honors, both as a junior in 2012. Frazier has played nine seasons in the [[NBA]], with eight different franchises.

==Early life==
Frazier was born on November 1, 1990, in [[Houston]], [[Texas]], to Billy and Janice. He started playing basketball when he was five years old. He would knock down the trophies of his sister and challenge his sister Krystal to games. His sister later said, "Most people learn basketball early on with a one-on-one kind of mentality... Tim at an early age didn't have that. He always wanted to make the team better and do whatever it takes to help the team out. He is such a true [[point guard]]." In his childhood, he was considered too small for contact sports but was noted for his quickness, which helped him thrive as a guard on the court.<ref>{{cite web|last=Snyder|first=Audrey|title=Injured Penn State guard Tim Frazier continues adapting to a season without basketball|url=http://www.pennlive.com/sports/index.ssf/2012/12/injured_penn_state_guard_tim_f.html|website=PennLive.com|date=December 26, 2012|access-date=September 27, 2014|archive-date=October 21, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141021101455/http://www.pennlive.com/sports/index.ssf/2012/12/injured_penn_state_guard_tim_f.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

== High school career ==
Frazier attended [[Strake Jesuit College Preparatory]] in Houston, Texas. He completed his junior year with 11.5 [[Point (basketball)|points]], 5.5 [[Rebound (basketball)|rebounds]], and 3.0 [[Steal (basketball)|steals]] per game. Frazier was named District 17-5A Defensive Player of the Year. In his senior season, he averaged 15.5 points, 7.7 rebounds, 5.5 [[Assist (basketball)|assists]], and 3.6 steals per game, leading the team to a 37–1 record.<ref name="psubio">{{cite web|title=Tim Frazier Bio|url=http://www.gopsusports.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/tim_frazier_475956.html|website=GoPSUSports.com|access-date=September 27, 2014|archive-date=December 21, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151221022744/http://www.gopsusports.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/tim_frazier_475956.html|url-status=live}}</ref> He, alongside fellow DI signees Joey Brooks & Steven Rogers, helped them become the first private school to reach the state tournament's semifinals. Frazier commented on his final year with Strake Jesuit in an interview with BlueWhiteIllustrated.com. "My game, I don't know, it just hit that next level," he said.<ref>{{cite web|last=Bauer |first=Nate |title=One on one with Tim Frazier |url=https://footballrecruiting.rivals.com/content.asp?CID=946964 |website=Rivals.com |publisher=BlueWhiteIllustrated.com |date=May 18, 2008 |access-date=September 27, 2014 |url-status=unfit |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141024051116/https://footballrecruiting.rivals.com/content.asp?CID=946964 |archive-date=October 24, 2014 }}</ref>

After completing his senior year with [[Strake Jesuit College Preparatory|Strake Jesuit]], Frazier was ranked the 20th-best [[point guard]] of his class, the 110th-most-valuable player overall, and a three-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]]. According to TexasHoops.com, he was the best recruit in the state, and the ''[[Houston Chronicle]]'' labeled him the Boys Basketball Player of the Year. Frazier played with the Houston Elite [[Amateur Athletic Union]] team, which had produced players such as Anthony Thompson, Eddren McCain and Chris Roberts, all of whom attended [[Bradley University]]. He graduated high school ''[[Latin honors|cum laude]]''.<ref name="psubio"/>

On October 23, 2008, Frazier verbally committed to the [[Penn State Nittany Lions basketball]] team. He said to [[Scout.com]], "I decided to be a Nittany Lion because I felt it was a great fit for me. Penn State has great academics as well as a great basketball team and that's what I was looking for." Frazier also said that he had a "great time" on his official visit and all his relatives supported the decision.<ref>{{cite web|last=Brennan|first=Mark|title=Texas Point Guard Picks PSU|url=http://pennstate.scout.com/2/804162.html|website=Scout.com|date=November 23, 2008|access-date=September 27, 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141021123405/http://pennstate.scout.com/2/804162.html|archive-date=October 21, 2014}}</ref> He received offers from various other schools across the country, including [[Bradley Braves men's basketball|Bradley]], [[Colorado State Rams men's basketball|Colorado State]], [[New Mexico State Aggies men's basketball|New Mexico State]], [[Santa Clara Broncos men's basketball|Santa Clara]], [[Stanford Cardinal men's basketball|Stanford]], [[Stephen F. Austin Lumberjacks basketball|Stephen F. Austin]], and [[UTEP Miners men's basketball|UTEP]]. Frazier was also visited by [[San Diego Toreros men's basketball|San Diego]], [[TCU Horned Frogs men's basketball|TCU]], and Penn State, spanning from September to October 2008.<ref>{{cite web|title=Tim Frazier Rivals|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Tim-Frazier-68201|website=Yahoo.com|access-date=September 27, 2014|archive-date=October 23, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141023205550/http://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Tim-Frazier-68201|url-status=live}}</ref> After the move was made official, head coach [[Ed DeChellis]] said, "We are very excited to have Tim join our program. He is a very fast, quick player with tremendous speed in the backcourt and a good shooter. He possesses the kind of athleticism that [[Stanley Pringle]] does. He can get in the lane and find open guys and is a great drive and kick passer and he can score. He is a very good on-the-ball defender and a tremendous athlete and we think he really solidifies our backcourt for the future."<ref>{{cite web|title=Houston's Tim Frazier Commits To Play For DeChellis And Nittany Lions|url=http://www.gopsusports.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/111208aab.html|website=GoPSUSports.com|date=November 12, 2008|access-date=September 27, 2014|archive-date=October 20, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141020110001/http://www.gopsusports.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/111208aab.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

==College career==

===Freshman===
[[File:Tim Frazier 2009.jpg|thumb|right|Frazier dribbles against [[Malcolm Delaney]] of [[Virginia Tech Hokies men's basketball|Virginia Tech]]]]
Prior to the start of his freshman year, Frazier recorded a team-high 34-inch [[Vertical jump|vertical]] in Penn State's preseason workouts. He also matched the 2009 [[NBA Draft Combine]] record, and surpassed the event's best lane agility time.<ref name="psubio"/> Frazier did not participate in Penn State's exhibition opener against [[Slippery Rock University|Slippery Rock]]. Coach DeChellis said, "Billy Oliver, Sasa [Borovnjak], Tim Frazier, Jermaine Marshall, they haven't played in this yet, so it was important just to get out there."<ref>{{cite web|title=Penn State & Battle Cruise In Exhibition Opener, 82–51, Over Slippery Rock|url=http://www.gopsusports.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/110609aaa.html|website=GoPSUSports.com|date=November 6, 2009|access-date=September 27, 2014|archive-date=October 20, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141020105755/http://www.gopsusports.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/110609aaa.html|url-status=live}}</ref> In his first official appearance against [[Penn Quakers men's basketball|Pennsylvania]], Frazier added 2 assists and 1 rebound in a scoreless performance. He was only allowed 8 minutes of play time.<ref>{{cite web|title=November 13, 2009 Pennsylvania vs Penn State|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/ncaa/boxscore/2009-11-13/Pennsylvania--at-Penn-State/18753|website=RealGM.com|date=November 13, 2009|access-date=September 27, 2014|archive-date=October 20, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141020213204/http://basketball.realgm.com/ncaa/boxscore/2009-11-13/Pennsylvania--at-Penn-State/18753|url-status=live}}</ref> He scored his first points against [[Robert Morris Colonials men's basketball|Robert Morris]] the following contest, with a game-high 19 points off the bench. He shot 6-of-11 from the field, and 4-of-5 on three-pointers. Frazier also contributed 3 assists, 2 rebounds, and 1 steal in 30 minutes on the court. DeChellis said, "(Tim) is a hard guy to contain. If he starts making perimeter shots, then we're that much better. We've seen him where he can make shots in practice and do pretty well. We just needed to get him some confidence and get him into the flow."<ref>{{cite web|title=Post Game Quotes Penn State 80, Robert Morris 61|url=http://www.gopsusports.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/111609aac.html|website=GoPSUSports.com|date=November 16, 2009|access-date=December 8, 2014|archive-date=September 24, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924023128/http://www.gopsusports.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/111609aac.html|url-status=live}}</ref> The game would remain a season high for him under the scoring category.<ref>{{cite web|title=Second Half Surge Leads Nittany Lions Past Robert Morris, 80–61|url=http://www.gopsusports.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/111609aaa.html|website=GoPSUSports.com|date=November 16, 2009|access-date=September 27, 2014|archive-date=October 20, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141020110100/http://www.gopsusports.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/111609aaa.html|url-status=live}}</ref> Frazier was awarded his first start as a [[shooting guard]] on November 22, 2009, against [[Davidson Wildcats men's basketball|Davidson]]; he registered 7 points, 5 rebounds, 3 assists, and 3 steals. He recorded a season-high 34 minutes. He finished the [[2009–10 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2009–10 season]] averaging 5.0 points, 2.3 rebounds, 2.4 assists, 0.7 steals, and 1.7 [[Turnover (basketball)|turnovers]]. He played in all 31 regular season games.<ref>{{cite web|title=Tim Frazier Game Logs|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/player/Tim-Frazier/GameLogs/3977/NCAA/2010/All|website=RealGM.com|access-date=September 27, 2014|archive-date=October 20, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141020213036/http://basketball.realgm.com/player/Tim-Frazier/GameLogs/3977/NCAA/2010/All|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Sophomore===
Frazier made his sophomore debut on November 7, 2010, in an exhibition game against [[East Stroudsburg University of Pennsylvania|East Stroudsburg]]. He added 10 points, 6 assists, and two steals. Frazier also recorded a team-high 4 turnovers. DeChellis commented, "Offensively we were poor tonight and we had too many turnovers ... something we've struggled with in practice."<ref>{{cite web|title=Nittany Lions Defeat East Stroudsburg, 66–52, in Exhibition|url=http://www.gopsusports.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/110710aaa.html|website=GoPSUSports.com|date=November 7, 2010|access-date=September 28, 2014|archive-date=October 20, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141020110549/http://www.gopsusports.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/110710aaa.html|url-status=live}}</ref> On November 12, 2010, Frazier made his second appearance as a sophomore with 6 points, 7 rebounds, 6 assists, and 1 steal. He shot 1-of-5 on field goals, while going a perfect 4-of-4 from the free-throw line. Frazier was named the game's starting shooting guard and was allowed 30 minutes of playing time.<ref name="Tim Frazier Game Logs">{{cite web|title=Tim Frazier Game Logs|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/player/Tim-Frazier/GameLogs/3977/NCAA/2011/All|website=RealGM.com|access-date=September 28, 2014|archive-date=October 20, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141020212926/http://basketball.realgm.com/player/Tim-Frazier/GameLogs/3977/NCAA/2011/All|url-status=live}}</ref> He made his first-ever appearance as Penn State's starting [[point guard]] on November 19 versus [[Fairfield Stags men's basketball|Fairfield]], and contributed 3 points, 4 rebounds, 7 assists, and 1 steal. The team's coach commented on Frazier's powerful defensive performance, "thought Tim Frazier did a very nice job defensively on the point guard for Fairfield who is a really good player. He bothered him all night."<ref>{{cite web|title=Postgame Quotes|url=http://www.gopsusports.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/111910aac.html|website=GoPSUSports.com|date=November 19, 2010|access-date=September 28, 2014|archive-date=October 20, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141020105856/http://www.gopsusports.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/111910aac.html|url-status=live}}</ref> Frazier made his first impression above the 10-point barrier on January 15, 2011, versus [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State]], with 11 points, 6 rebounds, and 5 assists. He shot 4-of-4 from the field and made three of four free throws. On March 12, 2011, Frazier scored 22 points against [[Michigan State Spartans men's basketball|Michigan State]], his season-high as a sophomore, helping the team pull off the upset victory in the semifinals of the [[2011 Big Ten Conference men's basketball tournament]].<ref name="Tim Frazier Game Logs"/> He played in his first [[NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] game against [[Temple Owls men's basketball|Temple]], contributing 15 points, 7 assists, 5 rebounds, and 2 steals. He made a late miscue guarding [[Juan Fernández (basketball, born 1990)|Juan Fernández]], allowing the opposing guard to close out the game with under one second remaining in regulation. Frazier recalled the moment, "I closed out high end so he wouldn't be able to shoot over me. (He) made a great move, pivoted a couple of times and then stepped through."<ref name="Associated Press">{{cite web|title=Fernandez's basket gives Temple 66–64 win over PSU|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/article/2011/03/17/AR2011031703420.html|website=WashingtonPost.com|publisher=Associated Press|date=March 17, 2011|access-date=September 28, 2014|archive-date=October 25, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141025053737/http://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/article/2011/03/17/AR2011031703420.html|url-status=live}}</ref> Fernández said, "I was thinking about shooting a jump shot but I killed my dribble and (Tim) Frazier was right there. For some reason he jumped over to my right and that gave me the space to go left."<ref name="Associated Press"/> By the end of the season, Frazier averaged 6.3 points, 5.1 assists, 3.9 rebounds, 1.0 steals, and 0.1 blocks per game. He was named to the Academic All-[[Big Ten Conference|Big Ten]] following [[2010–11 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2010–11]].<ref name="psubio"/>

===Junior===
[[File:Tim Frazier vs Hartford.jpg|thumb|right|Frazier shoots a three-pointer vs [[Hartford Hawks men's basketball|Hartford]] in 2011]]
Frazier opened his junior season, and his first year under coach [[Pat Chambers]], on November 5, 2011, in an exhibition game against [[Slippery Rock University|Slippery Rock]]. He led the team in scoring with 19 points. Frazier also posted 7 assists and 6 rebounds, helping Penn State win the game 64–47.<ref>{{cite web|title=Nittany Lions Down Slippery Rock, 64–47|url=http://www.gopsusports.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/110511aaa.html|website=GoPSUSports.com|date=November 5, 2011|access-date=September 30, 2014|archive-date=October 6, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141006150115/http://www.gopsusports.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/110511aaa.html|url-status=live}}</ref> He took part in the Nittany Lions' first regular season contest on November 12 against [[Hartford Hawks men's basketball|Hartford]], with 12 points, 6 assists, and 5 steals in spite of being given 28 minutes on the court. When asked on his communication with Frazier, Chambers said, "I'm telling him to make plays ... he has to be one of our leading scorers. He's got to look to score."<ref>{{cite web|title=Nittany Lions Down Hartford, 70–55|url=http://www.gopsusports.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/111211aaa.html|website=GoPSUSports.com|date=November 12, 2011|access-date=September 30, 2014|archive-date=October 6, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141006100437/http://www.gopsusports.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/111211aaa.html|url-status=live}}</ref> In the following game, Frazier made his second career display with 20 or more points. He also matched his career-high total on assists, with 10. This was his second [[double-double]] with Penn State. Frazier also finished with 6 rebounds, 3 steals, and 1 block. Chambers said in a post-game interview, "I'm very greedy. I'm an old point guard, so I want more out of Tim Frazier, if you can imagine ... what more means is even more leadership, even better habits. We're always trying to create the best habits we can for the most difficult situation.".<ref name="gopsusports.com">{{cite web|title=Frazier Leads Lions Past Radford, 62–46|url=http://www.gopsusports.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/111411aac.html|website=GoPSUSports.com|date=November 14, 2011|access-date=September 30, 2014|archive-date=October 6, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141006081846/http://www.gopsusports.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/111411aac.html|url-status=live}}</ref> Frazier helped power the 62–46 victory over [[Radford Highlanders men's basketball|Radford]], the team's second consecutive win in the regular season. It was also Penn State's first-round game in the [[Hall of Fame Tip-Off]] tournament.<ref name="gopsusports.com"/> In his next game against [[LIU Sharks men's basketball|LIU–Brooklyn]], Frazier scored a career-high 26 points and matched his assists record for the second straight game, with 10. It was his second straight double-double and the third in his stint with Penn State. Chambers commented after the game, "Tim was terrific. He was a great leader tonight. He did everything you ask your point guard to do tonight." He helped the program reach a 3–0 record for the third time in 12 seasons.<ref>{{cite web|title=Penn State Surges Past Long Island, 77–68|url=http://www.gopsusports.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/111611aaa.html|website=GoPSUSports.com|date=November 16, 2011|access-date=September 30, 2014|archive-date=November 19, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111119023038/http://www.gopsusports.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/111611aaa.html|url-status=live}}</ref> Following up on a loss to [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]], Frazier recorded 27 points on November 20, 2011, against [[South Florida Bulls men's basketball|South Florida]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Penn State Takes Down South Florida, 53–49|url=http://www.gopsusports.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/112011aaa.html|website=GoPSUSports.com|date=November 20, 2011|access-date=September 30, 2014|archive-date=November 23, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111123030050/http://www.gopsusports.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/112011aaa.html|url-status=live}}</ref> The next game, Frazier recorded a career-high 11 assists en route to his 4th double-double in 2011.<ref>{{cite web|title=Frazier Leads Lions Past YSU, 82–71|url=http://www.gopsusports.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/112311aab.html|website=GoPSUSports.com|date=November 23, 2011|access-date=September 30, 2014|archive-date=October 6, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141006155450/http://www.gopsusports.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/112311aab.html|url-status=live}}</ref> On January 11, 2012, Frazier scored a career-high 30 points against [[Nebraska Cornhuskers men's basketball|Nebraska]], with his team losing the game, 70–58. He led the Big Ten with eight 20-point games through the course of the year.<ref>{{cite web|title=Nittany Lions Fall to Nebraska, 70–58|url=http://www.gopsusports.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/011112aaa.html|website=GoPSUSports.com|date=January 11, 2012|access-date=September 30, 2014|archive-date=October 6, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141006100920/http://www.gopsusports.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/011112aaa.html|url-status=live}}</ref> By the end of the season, Frazier averaged 18.8 points, 6.2 assists, 4.7 rebounds, 2.4 steals, and 0.2 blocks. It was his highest scoring average with Penn State. He was named the John Lawther Team MVP, second-team NABC All-District, first-team [[List of All-Big Ten Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big Ten]], Academic All-Big Ten, Basketball Times' All-District, and Big Ten All-Defensive Team.<ref name="psubio"/>

===Redshirt===
Frazier began his fourth season representing Penn State with 17 points, 8 assists, and 5 rebounds in an exhibition game against [[Philadelphia University|Philadelphia]] on November 3, 2012. He sat out for much of the second half, giving his duties to D. J. Newbill. After the game, Frazier said that the team "just played Penn State basketball."<ref>{{cite web|title=Nittany Lions Defeat Philadelphia, 79–54|url=http://www.gopsusports.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/110312aaa.html|website=GoPSUSports.com|date=November 3, 2012|access-date=September 30, 2014|archive-date=October 6, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141006140241/http://www.gopsusports.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/110312aaa.html|url-status=live}}</ref> On November 9, 2012, the first regular season for Frazier as a senior, he logged his 19th career 20-point game against [[Saint Francis Red Flash men's basketball|Saint Francis (PA)]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Penn State Downs Saint Francis, 65–58|url=http://www.gopsusports.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/110912aaa.html|website=GoPSUSports.com|date=November 9, 2012|access-date=September 30, 2014|archive-date=October 6, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141006095657/http://www.gopsusports.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/110912aaa.html|url-status=live}}</ref> On November 18, Frazier left six minutes into a game against [[Akron Zips men's basketball|Akron]] due to a ruptured left [[Achilles tendon]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Tim Frazier out for year with injury|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/8656683/tim-frazier-penn-state-nittany-lions-year-injury|website=ESPN.com|date=November 20, 2012|access-date=September 30, 2014|archive-date=October 6, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141006093630/http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/8656683/tim-frazier-penn-state-nittany-lions-year-injury|url-status=live}}</ref> It was announced that he had a recovery period of about 12 months and would be out for the season. The injury was described as a "devastating blow" to the program by [[ESPN.com]] writer Eamonn Brennan. Chambers addressed the situation, saying, "I have no doubt he will meet this challenge and will again be one of the top players in the nation," in accordance to his potential fifth year of [[NCAA]] eligibility. Frazier [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirted]] the season shortly after it was announced by the school that he would undergo surgery.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Norlander|first1=Matt|title=Penn State loses star PG Tim Frazier for the season with Achilles injury|url=http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/eye-on-college-basketball/21071553/penn-state-loses-star-pg-tim-frazier-for-the-year-with-achilles-injury|website=CBSSports.com|date=November 20, 2012|access-date=September 30, 2014|archive-date=October 6, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141006081306/http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/eye-on-college-basketball/21071553/penn-state-loses-star-pg-tim-frazier-for-the-year-with-achilles-injury|url-status=live}}</ref> He said, "I will never forget that game, that injury, never forget that camera. I'm sitting there on the sideline with the (television) camera just zooming in on my foot. I'll never forget the look on my sister's face, my mom and dad's face." During his rehabilitation, Frazier began using the elliptical machine, doing work in the swimming pool, and taking part in [[weight training]]. He was guided by Penn State's athletic trainer, Jon Salazer, throughout the process. Frazier's sister Krystal had torn her right Achilles tendon when playing college basketball nearly seven years prior, and had gone through a similar rehabilitation before resuming her playing career.<ref>{{cite web|last=Rice|first=Jeff|title=Frazier helping while healing|url=https://247sports.com/college/penn-state/article/penn-state-receiving-assist-from-injured-guard-tim-frazier-116457/|website=247Sports.com|date=February 13, 2013|access-date=September 30, 2014|archive-date=February 18, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130218070301/http://pennstate.247sports.com/Article/Penn-State-receiving-assist-from-injured-guard-Tim-Frazier-116457|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Senior===
[[File:Chambers Watches the Game Unfold.jpg|thumb|left|Chambers speaks to Frazier on the sidelines.]]
In late April, it was made official that Frazier would return to [[Penn State Nittany Lions basketball|Penn State]] for his final year of eligibility. After the Big Ten granted him permission to partake his fifth season, Chambers said, "We are thrilled for him that he will have the opportunity to finish his career strong and again place himself among the top players in the nation."<ref name="cbssports.com">{{cite web|last1=Norlander|first1=Matt|title=Penn State's Tim Frazier will get one more year with the team|url=http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/eye-on-college-basketball/22132345/penn-states-tim-frazier-will-get-one-more-year-with-the-team|website=CBSSports.com|date=August 24, 2013|access-date=September 30, 2014|archive-date=October 6, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141006093248/http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/eye-on-college-basketball/22132345/penn-states-tim-frazier-will-get-one-more-year-with-the-team|url-status=live}}</ref> It was also announced that Frazier would pursue a second major over the summer.<ref name="cbssports.com"/>

On November 3, 2013, Frazier posted 11 points, 6 assists, 1 steal, and 1 block in a winning effort in an exhibition game against [[Northwood University|Northwood]]. In his first regular season game, he recorded a double-double against the [[Wagner Seahawks men's basketball|Wagner Seahawks]]. It was the seventh incident in Frazier's collegiate career. He was 12-for-17 on free-throws and added 4 assists.<ref>{{cite web|title=Frazier, Newbill Lead Lions Past Seahawks, 74–62, in Season Opener|url=http://www.gopsusports.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/110913aaa.html|website=GoPSUSports.com|date=November 9, 2013|access-date=September 30, 2014|archive-date=September 26, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140926025046/http://www.gopsusports.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/110913aaa.html|url-status=live}}</ref> On November 16, 2013, he scored a season-high 29 points against Pennsylvania, also recording 7 assists, 3 rebounds, and 2 steals. The duo of Frazier and D. J. Newbill was regarded as one of the nation's best backcourts, combining for 48 points through the contest.<ref>{{cite web|title=Penn State Downs Penn, 83–71|url=http://www.gopsusports.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/111613aab.html|website=GoPSUSports.com|date=November 16, 2013|access-date=September 30, 2014|archive-date=October 6, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141006102618/http://www.gopsusports.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/111613aab.html|url-status=live}}</ref> He matched his season record against [[St. John's Red Storm men's basketball|St. John's]] on November 29, 2013, posting 29 points.<ref>{{cite web|title=Penn State Outlasts St. John's in OT, 89–82|url=http://www.gopsusports.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/112913aaa.html|website=GoPSUSports.com|date=November 29, 2013|access-date=September 30, 2014|archive-date=October 6, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141006152027/http://www.gopsusports.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/112913aaa.html|url-status=live}}</ref> Over a week later, against [[Duquesne Dukes men's basketball|Duquesne]], Frazier recorded a career-high 13 assists, powering a 9-point victory for Penn State. His performance tied [[Dan Earl]] for the third-most assists in one game representing the Nittany Lions.<ref>{{cite web|title=Postgame Notes: Penn State 68, Duquesne 59|url=http://www.gopsusports.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/121113aaf.html|website=GoPSUSports.com|date=December 11, 2013|access-date=September 30, 2014|archive-date=October 6, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141006075346/http://www.gopsusports.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/121113aaf.html|url-status=live}}</ref> Frazier completed his final season with Penn State by averaging 14.9 points, 4.5 rebounds, 5.4 assists, 1.6 steals, and 0.2 blocks per game. He started in all 34 games, averaging 35.2 minutes.<ref>{{cite web|title=Tim Frazier Player Profile|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/player/Tim-Frazier/Summary/3977|website=RealGM.com|access-date=September 30, 2014|archive-date=October 6, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141006224129/http://basketball.realgm.com/player/Tim-Frazier/Summary/3977|url-status=live}}</ref> Frazier was named to the [[Bob Cousy Award]] watch list, third-team All-Big Ten, and the Barclays Center Classic all-tourney team. He was also a Senior CLASS Award finalist, and won the Big Ten Sportsmanship Award.<ref name="psubio"/>

=== Portland Trail Blazers (2015–2016) ===

On December 21, he started in his first game for the Trail Blazers in place of the injured [[Damian Lillard]]. Tim Frazier graduated in May 2013 with a 3.1 [[grade point average]] in supply chain and information systems at [[Smeal College of Business]]. Frazier added a second [[bachelor's degree]] in communication arts and sciences the following year. He later served as the basketball team's representative to the Penn State Student Athlete Advisory Board and was a member of the secret society Parmi Nous while at Penn State.<ref name="psubio"/> In March 2023, Frazier had his first child.
